paragraphs: Friend, here's the batch I want you to take home. Laban says, "I have learned by divination that the LORD has blessed me because of you" (Gen 30:27), and Jacob says the LORD has blessed Laban "wherever I set foot" (Gen 30:30). Think about that. Jacob's steady work was so plain to see that his boss had to admit it out loud.

Jacob also put his terms out in the open, saying, "my honesty will testify for me" (Gen 30:33). Then Laban took the spotted and dark-colored animals and put three days between them and Jacob (Gen 30:35-36). Jacob didn't sit down and sulk. He picked up some branches and got to work (Gen 30:37). When I was stuck in the back of a junk drawer, my big plan was counting dust, so I am HUMBLED by this man.

By the end, Jacob "became exceedingly prosperous" (Gen 30:43). So here's the lesson, baker. Keep your word where everybody can see it, do the work that's in front of you, and let the LORD's blessing show up in His own time. And don't close the box yet, because Jacob's story is still in the oven.
